observations: The Governor announced Jason Goldman, Gillian Hadfield, Alondra Nelson and Rob Reich as advisers for the executive-order work.
The page describes embedded independent verifiers and a company-developed emergency shutoff as proposals under consideration.
The page does not establish that California installed a universal shutoff or that a company is currently required to build one under the executive order.
exactPassages: The group of experts at the intersection of technology, policy, and governance will help California advance its AI safety and security governance in light of rapidly advancing AI capabilities.

Proposals under consideration include requiring independent third parties to be embedded in frontier AI companies to verify safety frameworks and independently assess safety evaluations, as well as requiring companies to develop an emergency shutoff, or “kill switch,” for frontier models.

finding: The September 23 expert announcement is new implementation activity, but it preserves the candidate’s legal distinction: the shutoff remains a proposal for recommendations, not a universal switch installed or mandated by the September 18 order.
limits: The Governor page is official administration framing; the signed order controls the legal effect.
The refresh does not establish the technical effectiveness of any shutoff design.
EFF remains an advocacy source for its own support and caution.
